# .white[The Challenge]

---

# The Traditional Systematic Review Challenge

.left-column[
### .oxford-blue[The Problem]
]

.right-column[
## Manual extraction from hundreds of papers

<br>

.large[
**📄 10+ data points per paper**
- Methodology, sample characteristics, key findings, effect sizes...

**📚 100-500+ papers per review**
- Typical scale for comprehensive systematic reviews

**⏰ ~30 hours of manual work**
- Opening PDFs → Searching → Copy-pasting → Repeat

**😰 Cognitive fatigue → errors**
- Inconsistent extraction across hundreds of papers
- Human attention degrades over repetitive tasks
]

<br>

### .center[.red[The Bottleneck:] .gray[Most time spent on mechanical extraction, not synthesis]]
]

???

Systematic literature reviews traditionally require researchers to manually extract data from each paper. This mechanical process consumes the majority of project time while offering minimal intellectual engagement. The real value—synthesis and analysis—gets compressed into whatever time remains.

---

class: inverse, center, middle
background-color: #002147

# .white[The Solution]

---

# A Multi-Stage Gemini-Powered Workflow

.panelset[

.panel[.panel-name[1. Scoping 🔍]

### Programmatic Literature Search

**Using Scopus API via R (rscopus package)**

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(rscopus)

# Search for relevant papers with structured query
results <- scopus_search(
    query = "(language OR reading) AND (imagery OR embodiment)",
    api_key = my_api_key,
    date = "2013-2025",
    view = "COMPLETE"
)

# Extract structured metadata
references <- extract_metadata(results)
# DOI, title, authors, abstract, year, journal, citations...
```

<br>

.pull-left[
**Benefits:**
- Reproducible search criteria
- Rich metadata captured automatically
- Scalable to hundreds of papers
]

.pull-right[
**Output:**
- Structured reference list (CSV)
- Ready for next workflow stage
- Includes DOIs for PDF retrieval
]
]

.panel[.panel-name[2. Curation 📥]

### Manual PDF Collection

.pull-left[
#### Process
- Download PDFs for each identified publication
- Organize files systematically
- Prepare for batch processing
]

.pull-right[
#### Quality Control
- Verify PDF completeness
- Check readability
- Remove duplicates
]

.center[**Critical:** This step ensures high-quality input for AI processing]
]

.panel[.panel-name[3. Extraction 🤖]

### NotebookLM: The Game-Changer

<br>

.pull-left[
### .red[Critical Discovery: Batch Size]

**✅ 30 PDFs per batch = Reliable**
- All papers processed
- Consistent output quality

**❌ >30 PDFs per batch = Data loss**
- Some papers silently omitted
- Incomplete extraction

**Solution:** Systematic batch processing workflow
]

.pull-right[
### .oxford-blue[Prompt Engineering is Paramount]

**Essential prompt elements:**
1. **Context:** Review domain and purpose
2. **Specific fields:** List every data point
3. **Output format:** CSV structure, column names
4. **Examples:** Show desired extraction style
5. **Edge cases:** How to handle missing data

**Result:** Detailed prompts prevent drift
]

<br>
<br>

.center[
.large[**Impact: 30+ hours of manual extraction → 3 hours of batch processing**]
]
]

.panel[.panel-name[4. Validation ✓]

### Human-in-the-Loop Quality Control

<br>

.pull-left[
#### .oxford-blue[Validation Protocol]

**1. Random Sampling**
- Check ~10% of extracted data points
- Stratified across different batches

**2. Direct Comparison**
- AI output vs. original papers
- Check for accuracy, completeness

**3. Error Assessment**
- Flag hallucinations
- Note omissions or misinterpretations

**4. Iteration**
- If unreliable: refine prompts
- .red[**Re-run ALL batches**] for consistency
]

.pull-right[
#### .green[Key Learnings]

**✓ Detailed prompts prevent drift**
- Specificity is inversely related to error rate

**✓ Consistency is crucial**
- Mixed prompt versions create noise
- Must re-process entire corpus after refinement

**✓ Structured outputs are more reliable**
- CSV format > free-form text
- Defined fields reduce hallucinations

**.red[✗ Never skip this step!]**
- Validation protects research integrity
]

<br>

.center[.large[**Critical Insight:** .oxford-blue[AI is a powerful accelerator, not an autopilot]]]
]

.panel[.panel-name[5. Synthesis 💡]

### Gemini for High-Level Analysis & Drafting

**Upload validated spreadsheet to Gemini for synthesis**

<br>

.pull-left[
#### .oxford-blue[Analytical Queries]

**Pattern identification:**
- "What are the most common methodologies?"
- "How have effect sizes changed over time?"
- "What sample characteristics are typical?"

**Gap analysis:**
- "What populations are underrepresented?"
- "Which methods have not been applied to X?"

**Comparative analysis:**
- "Compare behavioral vs. neuroimaging studies"
- "Contrast findings across age groups"
]

.pull-right[
#### .green[Drafting Support]

**Structure generation:**
- Draft introduction framing the gap
- Summarize methodological trends
- Create comparison tables

**Initial text:**
- "Draft an introduction explaining why individual differences in imagery matter for semantic processing"
- First drafts that you refine and enhance

**Note:** .gray[AI drafts require substantial human revision]
]

<br>
<br>

.center[.large[
**Fundamental shift:** .gray[Data extractor] → .oxford-blue[Data synthesizer & analyst]
]]
]

.panel[.panel-name[6. Finalization ✍️]

### Human-Led Writing & Critical Analysis

<br>

.large[
**Where human expertise is irreplaceable:**

**🎯 Critical interpretation**
- Evaluating study quality and validity
- Identifying methodological limitations

**📊 Nuanced synthesis**
- Reconciling contradictory findings
- Weighing evidence quality, not just quantity

**🔗 Contextual integration**
- Connecting findings to theoretical frameworks
- Situating within disciplinary conversations

**✨ Original contributions**
- Novel insights and perspectives
- Identifying implications and future directions

**🎓 Academic rigor**
- Disciplinary expertise and judgment
- Responsible, ethical scholarship
]

<br>

.center[.large[
.green[**Optimal approach:**] .gray[AI handles mechanical tasks] + .oxford-blue[Humans drive intellectual work]
]]
]

]

.pull-left[

- Documented validation procedures

# .white[Key Learnings]

---

# Practical Lessons: What Works & What Doesn't

.panelset[

.panel[.panel-name[Prompt Engineering 🎯]

## The Foundation of Reliable Output

<br>

.pull-left[
### .green[✅ What Works]

**1. Detailed Context**
- Explain the research domain
- State the review's purpose
- Define key concepts

**2. Explicit Structure**
- Specify exact output format (CSV)
- List all column names
- Define data types

**3. Comprehensive Instructions**
- Enumerate every data point to extract
- Provide extraction examples
- Explain edge case handling

**4. Quality Guidance**
- "If not reported, leave blank"
- "Extract exact text, do not paraphrase"
- "One row per experiment/study"
]

.pull-right[
### .red[❌ What Fails]

**Vague prompts:**
- "Extract data from these papers"
- Result: Inconsistent, incomplete output

**Assumed knowledge:**
- Using domain jargon without definition
- Result: Misinterpretation of concepts

**Unspecified format:**
- "Summarize the findings"
- Result: Unstructured, unusable output

**Missing edge cases:**
- No guidance for missing data
- Result: Hallucinated values

<br>

### .oxford-blue[Key Principle]
**Prompt specificity inversely correlates with error rate**
]

<br>

.center[.large[**Bottom Line:** .oxford-blue[Invest time upfront in prompt design—it pays dividends]]]
]

.panel[.panel-name[Technical Limits 🚧]

## Discovered Boundaries

### NotebookLM Constraints

.pull-left[
**Batch Processing:**
- ✓ 30 PDFs per batch = Reliable
- ✗ >30 PDFs per batch = Data loss
- Solution: Systematic batch workflow
]

.pull-right[
**File Quality Matters:**
- Scanned PDFs reduce accuracy
- Clear, well-formatted papers work best
- Pre-screening improves outcomes
]

### Workarounds Developed

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# Batch processing function
process_in_batches <- function(pdf_list, batch_size = 30) {
    batches <- split(pdf_list, ceiling(seq_along(pdf_list) / batch_size))
    results <- lapply(batches, upload_to_notebookLM)
    return(bind_rows(results))
}
```
]

.panel[.panel-name[Validation is Critical ✓]

## Human Oversight Required

.large[
### The 10% Rule

- Manually check **~10% of extracted data**
- Compare against original papers
- Flag errors, hallucinations, omissions
- **If unreliable:** Refine prompts and re-run ALL batches

### Why Re-run Everything?
- Ensures **consistency** across the entire dataset
- Prevents mixed-quality data
- Maintains methodological rigor

### Unexpected Finding
Initially skeptical, I was .green[**pleasantly surprised**] by accuracy after proper prompt refinement
]
]

.panel[.panel-name[Expectations vs Reality 📊]

## From Skepticism to Integration

<br>

.pull-left[
### .gray[Initial Expectations (Low)]

**My concerns before starting:**

😟 **Hallucination risk**
- Would AI fabricate data?
- Could I trust any of the output?

🤔 **Batch processing skepticism**
- Would it handle 100+ papers reliably?
- Would quality degrade at scale?

😰 **Consistency fears**
- Would outputs be comparable across batches?
- Would I need manual harmonization?

🚫 **Expected minimal use**
- Planned to use AI sparingly
- Would rely primarily on manual methods
]

.pull-right[
### .green[Actual Experience (Exceeded)]

**Reality after proper prompt engineering:**

✅ **High accuracy achieved**
- ~90% accuracy with refined prompts
- Hallucinations rare and detectable

✅ **Reliable at scale**
- Successfully processed 500+ papers
- Consistent quality across batches

✅ **Major time savings realized**
- 30+ hours saved per review
- Quality maintained or improved

✅ **Now central to workflow**
- Integrated into standard practice
- Would not return to purely manual methods

<br>

### .oxford-blue[Critical Success Factor]
**Investment in prompt engineering** transformed
performance from unusable to exceptional
]
]

]

# Appendix: Impact Metrics

```{r impact-metrics, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Create comparison data
metrics <- data.frame(
    Task = rep(c("Data Extraction", "Analysis & Synthesis", "Writing & Refinement"), 2),
    Approach = rep(c("Traditional", "Gemini-Powered"), each = 3),
    Hours = c(
        30, 10, 10, # Traditional
        3, 12, 10
    ) # Gemini-powered
)

ggplot(metrics, aes(x = Task, y = Hours, fill = Approach)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
        "Traditional" = "#8B8B8B",
        "Gemini-Powered" = "#002147"
    )) +
    labs(
        title = "Time Allocation Comparison",
        subtitle = "Traditional vs. Gemini-Powered Literature Review Workflow",
        y = "Hours per Review",
        x = ""
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#002147"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "#666666"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 12)
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Hours),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
        vjust = -0.5,
        size = 4
    )
```

.center[.large[.oxford-blue[**Total time reduced from 50 hours → 25 hours**]]]
.center[.gray[More importantly: Time shifted from manual extraction to high-value synthesis]]
